notes: Example configuration generated by the CraneCalc configurator; fictitious crane, supplier, site and owner data, to be replaced with project data. Scope: 1 simply supported 30-ft bay, W36X282 girder, one 30-ton cab crane, on new freestanding W14X342 columns with rolled W-stub brackets, base plates, anchor rods and spread footings, and crane-level rod X-bracing; the existing building carries no crane load. Seismic: ordinary steel cantilever column system across the runway and rod bracing not specifically detailed for seismic resistance along it, Seismic Design Category B. Bumper overhang assumed 20 in (end-wheel centerline to the extended bumper face, a typical supplier proportion): the stop contact positions use it; confirm with the crane supplier. The bracket stays: the W10X60 crane-level strut is moment-connected in plan at every column by 0.5 in plates on its flanges (torsion brace, 4 rows of bolt pairs) and holds the new W14X342 columns against the twist: 0.0240 rad factored (limit 0.02) and 0.305 in of bearing movement at every crane start and stop (limit 0.514 in), still beyond a limit (column-twist or column-twist-rotation fails and stays in the calculation: a stiffer strut, a torsionally stiffer column or a column cap is needed). With the strut on the column centerline alone, the girder seated 36.75 in off the column axis, the traction twists the column 0.0853 rad factored (limit 0.02) and 1.085 in of bearing movement at every crane start and stop (limit 0.514 in). The strut is sized so the girder's twist movement under the factored traction stays within 0.063 in (a configurator target, tightened from 1/8 in where the tie could not take the movement, so the tie, slots and gaps are not sized by it).

selections.reason: The support reaction, about 80 kip, is above the AIST TR-13 §5.9.2 guideline of 50 kip for column brackets, a clause to be verified: consider column caps over the new columns; an advisory, not a code limit, so the support entered (Rolled W-stub bracket) is kept and checked here.

A direct flange saddle does not suit this rolled girder (the sized saddle leaves saddle-across-fatigue 1.48, flange-tie-weld-fatigue 0.97 for the estimated tie demands; a welded saddle is a Category D/E attachment on the top flange of this high-cycle runway (CMAA Class D, AIST Class C)): the paired flat bars bolt to the tie-side bearing stiffener, cut as one plate with its gusset extension past the flange tip (no weld at the gusset), the full-depth stiffener pair carrying the tie force into the girder.

Lightest compact W within the sizing targets (ratio ≤ 0.85, deflections ≤ 0.9 of the limits): top-flange tip stress (DG7, warping and second-order twist) ratio 0.81, vertical deflection 0.28 and lateral 0.67 of their limits; flanges at least 10.5 in wide for the end bearing bolt gauge and the rail seat; lighter candidates rejected: 85 by sizing ratio, 63 by flange width; the next lighter, W27X281: tips ratio 0.99 > 0.85. These are the configurator's screening estimates (a simplified model that ranks the catalog), not the final ratios: the calculation checks the section and reports its own ratios.

New cantilever column for a 30-ton crane (W14X120 to 5 t, W14X159 to 12.5 t, W14X211 to 25 t, else W14X257). The W14X257 chosen for the crane gives base drift ratio 1.18 > 0.9: the lightest heavier W14 within the drift and torsion ratios.
Set by the tie sizing: the column face moves out from 20 in (to at most 30 in) until the tie passes its imposed-movement and strength checks.

fabrication.steel: Girder ASTM A992; plates, bars and stiffeners ASTM A572 Grade 50 unless noted.
fabrication.bolting: ASTM F3125 Grade A325, pretensioned, Class B faying surfaces, standard holes unless slots are detailed. Sliding-end bearing bolts and column-end tie bolts pretensioned against steel sleeves.
fabrication.welding: E70XX low-hydrogen electrodes per AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020, cyclically loaded provisions. Continuous fillets as dimensioned; no intermittent welds on cyclic load paths. Smooth starts and stops.
fabrication.inspection: Visual inspection of all welds; AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020 cyclically loaded acceptance criteria; magnetic particle testing of fillets at fatigue-sensitive attachments; 100% ultrasonic testing of CJP welds; bolt pretension verification per RCSC.
fabrication.erection: Set and level the bearings, install the end bearings and flange ties, then set the rails. Provide temporary restraint until the permanent ties are complete.
fabrication.railAlignment: Set the rails to the specified gauge, alignment and level tolerances and survey them after erection, before the load test.
